The Best Kid-Friendly Restaurants in Houston

Burgers, pizza, chicken tenders, and entertainment for them. Cocktails and good stuff for you.

by Brianna McClane and Brittany Britto Garley
Updated Sep 4, 2026, 2:00 PM EDT

Everyone’s gotta eat, but dining out with kids can be daunting. Young diners often need approachable food, plenty of elbow room, and some form of entertainment (and the adults might appreciate a cocktail or two). But going to a restaurant with kids shouldn’t mean sacrificing a quality meal.

Fortunately, Houston is home to a bounty of restaurants where kids can be kids and the food is good too. Some come equipped with playgrounds, games, and toys, while others offer kid-friendly menus alongside food and drinks that appeal to grown-ups. Here are some of Houston’s best bets for dining out with the whole family.

by Brianna McClane and Brittany Britto Garley
Updated Sep 4, 2026, 2:00 PM EDT

Everyone’s gotta eat, but dining out with kids can be daunting. Young diners often need approachable food, plenty of elbow room, and some form of entertainment (and the adults might appreciate a cocktail or two). But going to a restaurant with kids shouldn’t mean sacrificing a quality meal.

Fortunately, Houston is home to a bounty of restaurants where kids can be kids and the food is good too. Some come equipped with playgrounds, games, and toys, while others offer kid-friendly menus alongside food and drinks that appeal to grown-ups. Here are some of Houston’s best bets for dining out with the whole family.

Jimmy Changas

Let the kids monkey around at the Jimmy’s Jungle playground, offered at all Jimmy Changas locations, while they wait for their meal. The Little Jimmy’s menu features quintessential Tex-Mex choices like cheese enchiladas, crispy tacos, or quesadillas, plus complimentary soft-serve ice cream and a drink. The restaurant’s multiple seating options are ideal for any party preference, from oversized booths to patio tables under umbrellas. Young artists can also submit their creations for a chance to have them featured on the kids’ menu.

  • 300 Westgreen Blvd, Katy, TX, 77450, US
  • (832) 321-5927
  • Visit Website
Jimmy Changas

Bellagreen

The CityCentre outpost of this popular restaurant is perfect for families looking to get some fresh air before, during, or after their meal. Bellagreen provides both indoor dining and patio seating, plus it conveniently faces the development’s green space, where children love to run wild. Highlights of the robust menu include spicy fish tacos and a honey-fried goat cheese and arugula salad. Bellagreen is a destination for those with food allergies and diet restrictions: Even the kids’ mac and cheese and chicken strips are gluten-free.

  • 800B Town and Country Blvd, Houston, TX, 77024, US
  • (713) 464-5557
  • Visit Website
Bellagreen

Feges BBQ

Barbecue is a Houston family favorite, so a visit to Feges in Spring Branch is bound to make everyone happy. Its kids’ menu is packed with beloved dishes like a corndog, a cheeseburger, and a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, all of which come with a choice of side and a complimentary cookie. A covered, enclosed playspace on the patio keeps the little ones entertained, while adults dig into plates laden with smoked meats. On Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 8 p.m., kids eat free with the purchase of an adult entree.

  • 8217 Long Point Rd, Houston, TX, 77055, US
  • (346) 319-5339
  • Visit Website
Julie Soefer Photography

Kenny & Ziggy’s

With a massive four-page menu that spans breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and charming booth and counter seating, this New York-style deli is a treat for both adults and children. Here, comforting dishes like matzoh ball soup and its famous chopped liver abound, as do weekly breakfast specials, all-beef hot dogs, burgers, and sandwiches stuffed with almost any protein imaginable. Dessert is particularly special. Enjoy a slice of cheesecake or pie, or opt for fountain creations like ice cream sodas, old-fashioned milkshakes, hot fudge sundaes, and more.

  • 1743 Post Oak Blvd, Houston, TX, 77056, US
  • (713) 871-8883
  • Visit Website
Kenny & Ziggy’s New York Delicatessen

The Best Classic Restaurants in Houston
Jun 30, 2025
The Best Classic Restaurants in Houston

Little Matt’s

There are kid-friendly restaurants, and then there are kid-focused restaurants, like this one. Current owners Bill and Cindy Lillard operate the restaurant in memory of their son, Bobby, who died of a rare disease at 8 years old. Entertainment abounds at this quaint neighborhood spot, which houses an iPad station, a candy counter spilling over with sweet treats, a photo booth, and an arcade. Kids aren’t the only ones having fun, though. Adults are treated to complimentary wine, beer, or margaritas. To make the outing even more meaningful, a portion of the restaurant’s proceeds goes to Texas Children’s Hospital.

  • 6203 Edloe St, Houston, TX, 77005, US
  • (713) 592-6200
  • Visit Website

Gaspachos Mexican Bites

Levy Park, one of the city’s most beloved local playgrounds, is even more inviting with this family-friendly kiosk, which makes it easy to turn a park visit into a full-day outing. The dedicated kids menu features crowd-pleasers like quesadillas, hot dogs, and fries, while refreshing treats such as shaved ice and smoothies round out the offerings.

  • 3709 Eastside St, Houston, TX, 77098, US
  • (832) 863-5243
  • Visit Website
Jay Ford

La Mex

For families with little early risers, La Mex’s 7 a.m. opening time is enticing, along with its kid’s pancake platter. Quesadillas, fajitas, tacos, and chicken strips served with a side of beans are on offer for lunch and dinner. Best of all, the restaurant is situated alongside an enclosed green space, meaning adults can sip on cocktails and chow down tacos while the little ones release some energy.

  • Order delivery from Grubhub
  • 1223 W 34th St Ste A100, Houston, TX, 77018, US
  • (713) 929-2783
  • Visit Website
Becca Wright

d’Alba

With a patio for al fresco dining, a welcoming playground, and an arcade, d’Alba is a restaurant both kids and adults can get behind. Enjoy wood-fired pizzas and handmade pasta dishes that can easily be shared. If the kids want their own meal, there are chicken fingers, pasta, cheese pizza, and a classic peanut butter and jelly served with fries. Cocktails like the Alba red mule with Deep Eddy Ruby Red vodka and hibiscus ginger beer keep the adults sweet, while the whole table can dig in to scoops of seasonal sorbet or freshly baked chocolate chip cookies.

  • Book a table
  • Order delivery from Grubhub
  • 3715 Alba Rd, Houston, TX, 77018, US
  • (346) 319-5790
  • Visit Website

Buttermilk Baby

Ben Berg’s playful rendition of the vintage soda fountain makes diners feel like a kid in a candy shop. Buttermilk Baby’s interior boasts vibrant hues, a life-sized carousel horse, an oversized sundae statue, and an ice cream bar with a sprinkle-filled center. Not only are buttermilk biscuits available, but the entire menu is kid-friendly with options like chicken sandwiches, burgers, chicken fingers, sweet potato fries, and grilled cheese. The true draw here is the dessert — Buttermilk Baby is the first Texas purveyor of Carvel ice cream. Choose from indulgent ice cream sandwiches, cakes, and soft serve, or an adult-only boozy milkshake.

  • 600 N Shepherd Dr, Houston, TX, 77007, US
  • (713) 840-1555
  • Visit Website
Alex Montoya

Nonno’s Pizza

This pizza joint is bound to please all ages, with thin crust, tavern-style pizza, and combinations including a Spam, pineapple, and jalapeño pie. The restaurant’s nostalgic vibe extends to a small arcade, ‘90s tunes played on a reel-to-reel machine (an educational moment for the littles), and vintage lamps in booth-style seating that harken back to the halcyon days of Pizza Hut.

  • 1613 Richmond Ave, Houston, TX, 77006, US
  • (713) 505-1018
Brittany Britto Garley

Clay’s Restaurant

Step back into the Wild West at this Katy institution that has been serving classic comfort food for almost 40 years. Step up to the counter to order classics like burgers, seafood platters, and the signature chicken fried steak. There’s plenty of seating inside the saloon-like dining room but parents want to be on the back patio, where the kids can run free in the Old West Town front. There’s also a large sandbox and coin-operated ride-on machines.

  • Order delivery from Grubhub
  • 17717 Clay Rd, Houston, TX, 77084, US
  • (281) 859-3773
  • Visit Website
Clay’s Restaurant

Barnaby’s Cafe

The Museum District outpost of this Houston cafe is perfect for family outings, and it’s just down the street from the Children’s Museum. Tykes can color, tinker with toy robots, or play games on the outdoor patio while waiting for their food. Kid-friendly eats include fried chicken sliders, bite-sized burgers, mini corn dogs, and mac and cheese, alongside desserts like Rice Krispie treats, or a cookie. For the adults, dishes include chicken fried steak, cobb salad, and baby back ribs.

  • 1801 Binz St, Houston, TX, 77004, US
  • (713) 874-1454
  • Visit Website

Saint Arnold Brewing Company

Kids will stay occupied at this local brewery thanks to its expansive outdoor beer garden, which is outfitted with a hedge maze, decorative art cars, corn hole, and an oversized fountain. The menu also offers plenty of finger foods and shareable dishes for all ages, including cheesy pizzas, tangy wings, soft pretzels served with queso blanco, and a variety of sandwiches. The extra-fizzy house-made root beer is a special treat, which can be easily transformed into a float with a scoop of Fat Cat ice cream. Work up an appetite at Meow Wolf right across the street before heading over to Saint Arnold’s for a cold pint.

  • 2000 Lyons Ave, Houston, TX, 77020, US
  • (713) 686-9494
  • Visit Website

Long Weekend

Families have plenty of room to spread out at this Heights-area restaurant, which features a massive outdoor play area where kids can burn off some energy while parents settle in with cocktails and a meal. Younger kids can head indoors to a dedicated creative space stocked with activities, making it easy for families with children of different ages to keep everyone entertained. The menu ranges from wagyu chicken fried steak to bowls of pozole, with plenty of options for younger diners, too.

  • Book a table
  • 2044 East T C Jester Boulevard, Houston, Texas 77008, United States
  • (713) 814-8978
  • Visit Website
Long Weekend

The Hottest New Restaurants in Houston
Sep 23
The Hottest New Restaurants in Houston

Recess River Oaks

At this new River Oaks spot, kids can play in the sleek indoor playground supervised by Recess staff while families tuck into plates of chicken piccata and steak frites in the second-level restaurant. Children three and under must have a caretaker with them at all times, while staff members with pediatric first aid and CPR training keep an eye on the older ones. It’s pay to play here, with a range of price points from hourly visits to monthly memberships. Reservations for both the playground and the restaurant are recommended, but not required.

  • 1500 Waugh Dr, Houston, TX, 77019, US
  • (832) 390-4660
  • Visit Website

The Pit Room

The Memorial location of this popular barbecue joint has an enclosed stretch of turf where kids can run around safely before chowing down on crowd favorites like mac and cheese. The menu extends beyond the standard slabs of brisket and ribs at this outpost, with grill offerings like hot dogs, burgers, wings, and fries. An ice cream counter stocked with giant tubs of Blue Bell tempts diners of all ages looking for dessert.

  • 10301-A Katy Freeway, Houston, Texas 77024
  • (281) 888-1929
  • Visit Website
